sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼等多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日于 NYTimes.com 上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: For weeks, tens of thousands of people have been taking to the streets of Belarus to demand the resignation of their president,
sentences.zh: 数周以来，成千上万的白俄罗斯民众走上街头，要求他们的总统辞职，

sentences.en: Aleksandra Lukashenko, today.
sentences.zh: 即今天的亚历山大·卢卡申科。

sentences.en: My colleague, Ivan Nitscheparenko, on how Europe's last dictator came to power and his fight to hold onto it.
sentences.zh: 我的同事伊万·尼切帕连科将讲述欧洲最后一位独裁者是如何掌权，以及他为保住权力所进行的斗争。

sentences.en: Wednesday, September 2nd.
sentences.zh: 9月2日，星期三。

sentences.en: Ivan, I know you're based in Russia, in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 伊万，我知道你常驻俄罗斯莫斯科。

sentences.en: So where are you now?
sentences.zh: 那么你现在在哪里？

sentences.en: I'm currently in Belarus.
sentences.zh: 我现在在白俄罗斯。

sentences.en: It's a country of about 9.5 million, sandwiched between Russia and the European Union.
sentences.zh: 这是一个拥有约950万人口的国家，夹在俄罗斯和欧盟之间。

sentences.en: I'm here to cover the contested re-election of the incumbent president, Alexander Lukashenko.
sentences.zh: 我在这里报道现任总统亚历山大·卢卡申科备受争议的连任选举。

sentences.en: In Belarus, President Alexander Lukashenko has won the presidential vote with 79.9%, according to the latest exit poll.
sentences.zh: 据最新的出口民调显示，在白俄罗斯，亚历山大·卢卡申科总统以79.9%的得票率赢得了总统大选。

sentences.en: His re-election has inspired people to protest against him because they felt that the result that was announced 80% in his favor is totally incongruent with reality.
sentences.zh: 他的连任激起了民众的抗议，因为他们认为宣布的80%支持率与现实完全不符。

sentences.en: International observers have never seen any of the elections in Belarus as free and fair.
sentences.zh: 国际观察员从未认为白俄罗斯的任何一场选举是自由和公正的。

sentences.en: And today there were also widespread reports of violations at the ballot box.
sentences.zh: 而且今天也有大量关于投票站违规行为的报道。

sentences.en: So saying that he has won with more than 80%, And nobody is going to believe that.
sentences.zh: 所以说他以超过80%的得票率获胜，没有人会相信这一点。

sentences.en: We see days of protests that are being violently cracked down by Lukashenko's very robust security service with rubber bullets and stun grenades and everything.
sentences.zh: 我们看到连日的抗议活动遭到卢卡申科极其强硬的安全部门的暴力镇压，使用了橡胶子弹、眩晕手榴弹等一切手段。

sentences.en: And during that time, Lukashenko himself is basically going quiet.
sentences.zh: 而在那段时间里，卢卡申科本人基本上保持沉默。

sentences.en: And we don't really know what is his interpretation of what's been going on because we think that maybe he's just going to resign.
sentences.zh: 我们并不真正了解他对所发生之事的解读，因为我们曾以为他可能会辞职。

sentences.en: And suddenly, on Saturday night, almost one week after the election day, we learned that he will actually give a rally gathering his supporters in the central Minsk.
sentences.zh: 突然，在选举日过去近一周后的周六晚上，我们得知他实际上要在明斯克市中心举行一场集会，召集他的支持者。

sentences.en: And what happens at that rally?
sentences.zh: 那场集会上发生了什么？

sentences.en: So as I come to the rally to the main independence square,
sentences.zh: 当我来到通往主要独立广场的集会现场时，

sentences.en: I walk through the side streets that lead to it and I see that there are all these coach buses parked on the sides with groups of people standing.
sentences.zh: 我穿过通往那里的侧街，看到路边停满了大巴车，还有成群的人站在那里。

sentences.en: So it becomes clear that people were bussed in and that many people, if not most of them, didn't come there at their own will.
sentences.zh: 很明显，这些人是被大巴拉来的，而且很多人，如果不是大多数人的话，并非出于自愿来到这里。

sentences.en: and shortly into the rally
sentences.zh: 集会开始不久，

sentences.en: Lukashenko himself takes the stage
sentences.zh: 卢卡申科本人登上了舞台，

sentences.en: and I was very curious to see what he was about to say because after what I saw on the streets the police used rubber bullets tear gas and stun grenades injuring many
sentences.zh: 我非常好奇他会说些什么，因为在我目睹了街头警察使用橡胶子弹、催泪瓦斯和眩晕手榴弹造成多人受伤之后，

sentences.en: and it would be interesting to see how he would justify it
sentences.zh: 看看他将如何为这些行为辩解会很有意思。

sentences.en: And what he did was actually the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但他所做的恰恰相反。

sentences.en: What he did, he said that I own this country, and these people in the opposition, they are rats and they are trash and they are foreign-paid conspirators
sentences.zh: 他所做的是，他说这个国家是我的，而这些反对派人士，他们是老鼠，是垃圾，是受外国资助的阴谋家，

sentences.en: who just want to subvert the stability that we have earned with sweat.
sentences.zh: 他们只想颠覆我们用汗水换来的稳定。

sentences.en: He says, and remember, if you destroy Lukashenko, if you destroy your first president, this will be the beginning of your end.
sentences.zh: 他说，记住，如果你摧毁了卢卡申科，如果你摧毁了你们的第一任总统，这将是你们末日的开始。

sentences.en: He was basically saying that I created your country and you should be so grateful that you should allow me to rule over you for the rest of my life.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在说，是我创造了这个国家，你们应该心存感激，让我统治你们余生。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yvonne, when Lukashenko says that he created Belarus, what does he mean?
sentences.zh: 伊万，当卢卡申科说他创造了白俄罗斯时，他是什么意思？

sentences.en: And is that accurate?
sentences.zh: 这准确吗？

sentences.en: Well, it is accurate in a sense, because, of course, he's the first president of this country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从某种意义上说是准确的，因为他当然是这个国家的第一任总统。

sentences.en: In Moscow, the hammer and sickle is lowered for the last time, and an era comes to an end.
sentences.zh: 在莫斯科，镰刀锤子旗最后一次降下，一个时代宣告终结。

sentences.en: The red flag of Soviet communism still flew last weekend, but it flew over a country that no longer exists.
sentences.zh: 上周末，苏联共产主义的红旗仍在飘扬，但它飘扬在一个已经不复存在的国家上空。

sentences.en: So Belarus becomes independent in 1991, when the Soviet Union collapses.
sentences.zh: 所以，1991年苏联解体时，白俄罗斯获得了独立。

sentences.en: And people are euphoric about acquiring independence, acquiring their own flag, their own identity,
sentences.zh: 人们对获得独立、拥有自己的旗帜、自己的身份感到欣喜若狂，

sentences.en: the ability to develop their own language.
sentences.zh: 并拥有了发展自己语言的能力。

sentences.en: But shortly after, they realized that democracy, for instance, that they've acquired also brings chaos.
sentences.zh: 但不久之后，他们意识到，例如他们所获得的民主也带来了混乱。

sentences.en: A significant portion of the elderly and youth in the country are not only living in poverty, but are barely surviving.
sentences.zh: 国内很大一部分老人和年轻人不仅生活在贫困中，甚至难以生存。

sentences.en: And the economy is not working well, because as the rest of the Soviet Union, the Belarusian economy was a planned economy with no market,
sentences.zh: 经济运行状况不佳，因为和苏联其他地区一样，白俄罗斯的经济是计划经济，没有市场，

sentences.en: with prices set up from a single center, from Moscow, essentially.
sentences.zh: 价格基本上是由莫斯科的单一中心设定的。

sentences.en: And now you need to transform this huge economy into a market economy.
sentences.zh: 现在你需要将这个庞大的经济体转型为市场经济。

sentences.en: And in the process, a lot of people in Belarus feel a lot of pain.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，白俄罗斯的许多人感到非常痛苦。

sentences.en: And the social welfare programs cannot even begin to keep up with the rate of inflation.
sentences.zh: 社会福利计划甚至无法跟上通货膨胀的速度。

sentences.en: Because factories begin to close, their salaries actually, they go down.
sentences.zh: 因为工厂开始倒闭，他们的工资实际上在下降。

sentences.en: And by 1994, they seem willing to exchange the freedoms they've earned.
sentences.zh: 到了1994年，他们似乎愿意用自己赢得的自由，

sentences.en: for a sense of stability that would bring peace to their families.
sentences.zh: 去换取一种能为家庭带来和平的稳定感。

sentences.en: So a presidential election is called the first one in the country's history.
sentences.zh: 于是，该国历史上第一次总统选举被提上日程。

sentences.en: And this is the time where young Alexander Lukashenko comes to the stage.
sentences.zh: 这就是年轻的亚历山大·卢卡申科登场的时刻。

sentences.en: And Ivan, who is Lukashenko in this moment?
sentences.zh: 伊万，当时的卢卡申科是什么样的人？

sentences.en: As people in Belarus struggling to figure out what a post-Soviet Belarus even looks like are realizing that they crave stability.
sentences.zh: 当白俄罗斯民众努力弄清楚后苏联时代的白俄罗斯究竟是什么样子时，他们意识到自己渴望稳定。

sentences.en: He is someone who comes from a very modest background,
sentences.zh: 他是一个出身非常卑微的人，

sentences.en: from a small town in eastern Belarus,
sentences.zh: 来自白俄罗斯东部的一个小镇，

sentences.en: who raises quickly through the ranks to become a collective farm manager and then engages into politics.
sentences.zh: 他迅速晋升为集体农庄经理，然后投身政界。

sentences.en: And he seems to be very driven and very charismatic.
sentences.zh: 他看起来非常有干劲，也非常有魅力。

sentences.en: And people listen to him.
sentences.zh: 人们愿意听他说话。

sentences.en: People like him, especially people in the villages who have suffered the moSt.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢他，尤其是那些受苦最深的农村地区的人们。

sentences.en: And he attempts to talk to them directly by telling them that I can improve your lives right now.
sentences.zh: 他试图直接与他们对话，告诉他们我能立刻改善你们的生活。

sentences.en: I can take your lives back to where they were when you enjoyed them so much, when the Soviet Union was kind of at the height of its power.
sentences.zh: 我可以让你们的生活回到你们曾经非常享受的状态，回到苏联处于权力巅峰的时候。

sentences.en: And so how do the people of Belarus respond to this campaign message, this kind of backward-looking, nostalgic Soviet message.
sentences.zh: 那么白俄罗斯人民是如何回应这一竞选信息的，这种怀旧的、向后看的苏联式信息？

sentences.en: They like it.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢它。

sentences.en: Radical anti-corruption crusader Alexander Lukashenko is poised for a clear win.
sentences.zh: 激进的反腐斗士亚历山大·卢卡申科有望获得明确的胜利。

sentences.en: With his country's economy in rapid decline,
sentences.zh: 随着国家经济迅速衰退，

sentences.en: Lukashenko has vowed to purge the top echelons of power and undo market reforMs.
sentences.zh: 卢卡申科誓言要清洗权力高层并撤销市场改革。

sentences.en: He wins the election and he quickly begins to deliver on his promises.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了选举，并迅速开始兑现他的承诺。

sentences.en: He increases people's salaries.
sentences.zh: 他提高了人们的工资。

sentences.en: He reintroduces state control over prices and he cancels many of the market economy reforms that were introduced before him.
sentences.zh: 他恢复了国家对价格的控制，并取消了在他之前引入的许多市场经济改革。

sentences.en: He stops privatization of government enterprises.
sentences.zh: 他停止了政府企业的私有化。

sentences.en: He keeps them in the hands of the state.
sentences.zh: 他将它们保留在国家手中。

sentences.en: And people are very happy because they feel the change immediately and their standards of living improve.
sentences.zh: 人们非常高兴，因为他们立刻感受到了变化，生活水平得到了提高。

sentences.en: What people fail to notice is that the main reason why he's able to deliver them was because Russia has been subsidizing, essentially,
sentences.zh: 人们没有注意到的是，他之所以能够实现这些，主要原因是俄罗斯一直在补贴，本质上是，

sentences.en: the Belarusian economy through a scheme that is called Oil for Kisses Scheme.
sentences.zh: 通过一种被称为“石油换亲吻”的计划来补贴白俄罗斯经济。

sentences.en: Oil for Kisses.
sentences.zh: 石油换亲吻。

sentences.en: That's very evocative.
sentences.zh: 这非常形象。

sentences.en: What does it mean?
sentences.zh: 这是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, it basically means that Russia, being an energy superpower,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这基本上意味着作为能源超级大国的俄罗斯，

sentences.en: was essentially giving Belarus large amounts of oil that Belarus could refine and sell it to European markets and keep the difference.
sentences.zh: 本质上是在给白俄罗斯提供大量的石油，白俄罗斯可以将其提炼并卖给欧洲市场，并保留差价。

sentences.en: So by doing that, Russia was essentially trying to tie Belarus to Moscow.
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，俄罗斯本质上是在试图将白俄罗斯与莫斯科捆绑在一起。

sentences.en: So Russia is using essentially free oil as a tether to this former republic, and in return, Russia gets the goodwill, the brotherhood, the kind of loyalty of Belarus.
sentences.zh: 所以俄罗斯实际上是在利用免费石油作为束缚这个前加盟共和国的纽带，作为回报，俄罗斯获得了白俄罗斯的好感、兄弟情谊和某种忠诚。

sentences.en: Well, also because the Belarusian leader realizes perfectly well that the well-being of his country and the goodwill of his citizens depends on that whole scheme.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也因为白俄罗斯领导人非常清楚地意识到，他国家的福祉和公民的好感都依赖于整个计划。

sentences.en: So he realizes that his own political existence depends on Russia.
sentences.zh: 所以他意识到他自己的政治生存依赖于俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And my sense, Ivan, is that during this period, the West, the United States in particular,
sentences.zh: 伊万，我的感觉是，在此期间，西方，特别是美国，

sentences.en: is watching all of these former Soviet republics very warily and trying to make sure that they don't slide back into old Soviet ways and that they don't get too close to Russia because they want to make sure that they stay on a path toward democracy.
sentences.zh: 一直在非常警惕地注视着所有这些前苏联加盟共和国，并试图确保它们不会滑回旧的苏联方式，也不会与俄罗斯走得太近，因为他们想确保它们保持在通往民主的道路上。

sentences.en: So how does that play out when it comes to Lukashenko and Belarus?
sentences.zh: 那么，当涉及到卢卡申科和白俄罗斯时，情况是如何发展的？

sentences.en: So what happens is that he realizes pretty quickly that this kind of weariness that you've described is an asset for him, that he can trade in between Russia and the West,
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是，他很快意识到你所描述的这种警惕对他来说是一种资产，他可以在俄罗斯和西方之间进行交易，

sentences.en: that he can dance between the two.
sentences.zh: 他可以在两者之间跳舞。

sentences.en: Praising and criticizing both and kind of alternating because Russia doesn't want him to go to the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 既赞美又批评双方，并交替进行，因为俄罗斯不希望他倒向西方，

sentences.en: And the West doesn't want him to go to Russia.
sentences.zh: 而西方也不希望他倒向俄罗斯。

sentences.en: And he can benefit on that.
sentences.zh: 他可以从中获益。

sentences.en: And he does that throughout his career masterfully.
sentences.zh: 他在整个职业生涯中都非常巧妙地做到了这一点。

sentences.en: For instance, in 1996...
The referendums over in the former Soviet Republic of Belarus.
sentences.zh: 前苏联加盟共和国白俄罗斯的公投结束了。

sentences.en: The controversy it whipped up still blows strong.
sentences.zh: 它引发的争议依然强烈。

sentences.en: He conducts a very controversial referendum.
sentences.zh: 他进行了一场极具争议的公投。

sentences.en: They give him far greater powers over Parliament, plus a fresh five-year term of office.
sentences.zh: 公投赋予了他对议会更大的权力，外加一个新的五年任期。

sentences.en: That increases his powers dramatically.
sentences.zh: 这极大地增加了他的权力。

sentences.en: The president said dictatorship allegations were groundless.
sentences.zh: 总统称有关独裁的指控毫无根据。

sentences.en: and basically becomes his first step toward acquiring dictatorial powers.
sentences.zh: 这基本上成为他获取独裁权力的第一步。

sentences.en: And Western powers ostracize him, essentially.
sentences.zh: 西方大国基本上将他排斥在外。

sentences.en: And the following year, he signs this Union State Agreement with Russia in a grand ceremony held inside the Kremlin's grand palace.
sentences.zh: 第二年，他在克里姆林宫大宫殿内举行的盛大仪式上，与俄罗斯签署了这份《联盟国家条约》。

sentences.en: Boris Yeltsin stressed that the integration treaty between Russia and neighboring Belarus allows both countries to retain their sovereignty.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯·叶利钦强调，俄罗斯与邻国白俄罗斯之间的整合条约允许两国保留各自的主权。

sentences.en: During that ceremony, the two presidents of Russia and Belarus,
sentences.zh: 在那次仪式上，俄罗斯和白俄罗斯的两位总统，

sentences.en: Lukashenko and President Yeltsin at the time, they kiss each other, which becomes this kind of very symbolic moment for the two countries.
sentences.zh: 当时的卢卡申科和叶利钦总统，他们互相亲吻，这成为了两国之间一种非常具有象征意义的时刻。

sentences.en: Belarus President Lukashenko sorely needs economic help.
sentences.zh: 白俄罗斯总统卢卡申科迫切需要经济援助。

sentences.en: His country's centrally planned Soviet-style economy is in even worse shape than Russia's.
sentences.zh: 他国家那种中央计划的苏联式经济状况甚至比俄罗斯还要糟糕。

sentences.en: Russia sees it as though it basically rebuilds its old empire again.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯将其视为重建旧帝国。

sentences.en: They say it's a good deal for both their countries.
sentences.zh: 他们说这对两国来说都是一笔好交易。

sentences.en: The West is not so sure.
sentences.zh: 西方对此并不确定。

sentences.en: And the West, of course, is watching closely what is happening
sentences.zh: 当然，西方也在密切关注正在发生的事情，

sentences.en: and becomes increasingly willing to accept Lukashenko with his new semi-dictatorial powers because they don't want him to be completely swallowed by Russia.
sentences.zh: 并越来越愿意接受拥有新半独裁权力的卢卡申科，因为他们不希望他被俄罗斯完全吞并。

sentences.en: They want Belarus to stay in an independent state.

sentences.zh: 而他监禁并驱逐出境的所有其他候选人，

sentences.en: they also supported her.
sentences.zh: 他们也支持她。

sentences.en: They said that she is going to be our united opposition candidate.
sentences.zh: 他们说她将是我们统一的反对派候选人。

sentences.en: So they threw their support behind her back.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把支持投向了她。

sentences.en: And apart from that,
sentences.zh: 除此之外，

sentences.en: The particular thing about Belarus is that polls are banned here.
sentences.zh: 白俄罗斯的一个特殊之处在于这里禁止民调。

sentences.en: You cannot have a poll.
sentences.zh: 你不能进行民意调查。

sentences.en: So there are no polls that would say what is actually Lukashenko's real approval rating.
sentences.zh: 所以没有民调能说明卢卡申科真正的支持率是多少。

sentences.en: But in the age of the internet, you can do polls online and multiple polls have been conducted.
sentences.zh: 但在互联网时代，你可以在线进行民调，并且已经进行了多次民调。

sentences.en: And some of them have shown the support for Mr. Lukashenko to be as low as 3%.
sentences.zh: 其中一些显示卢卡申科先生的支持率低至3%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So it very much seems like she might be able to pull this off.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来她很有可能成功。

sentences.en: She might be able to beat Lukashenko.
sentences.zh: 她可能真的能击败卢卡申科。

sentences.en: Yeah, but what happened in reality was that when the results get announced, Lukashenko gets 80% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 是的，但现实中发生的情况是，当结果公布时，卢卡申科获得了80%的选票。

sentences.en: And of course, people realize that the whole election was just rigged.
sentences.zh: 当然，人们意识到整个选举只是被操纵了。

sentences.en: So what they do is they come out to protest en masse.
sentences.zh: 所以他们走上街头大规模抗议。

sentences.en: But it seems that Mr. Lukashenko, he expected this result, that this is what is going to happen, that people will come out.
sentences.zh: 但看起来卢卡申科先生预料到了这个结果，预料到会发生这种情况，预料到人们会走上街头。

sentences.en: Because as soon as people arrive to the scene of the rally,
sentences.zh: 因为就在人们到达集会现场时，

sentences.en: almost immediately, huge armored police vans come in.
sentences.zh: 几乎立刻，巨大的装甲警车就开了过来。

sentences.en: And the people, they are not even doing much.
sentences.zh: 而人们甚至什么都没做。

sentences.en: They're standing on sidewalks, clapping.
sentences.zh: 他们只是站在人行道上鼓掌。

sentences.en: And the thing you have to realize about Mr. Lukashenko's Belarus is that even if you clap in a group of five on the sidewalk, you will be detained.
sentences.zh: 关于卢卡申科先生的白俄罗斯，你必须意识到，即使你只是在人行道上五个人一组地鼓掌，也会被拘留。

sentences.en: and probably even beaten by police wow and you have this riot policeman in full gear appear on
sentences.zh: 甚至可能被警察殴打。哇，你看到全副武装的防暴警察出现在

sentences.en: the scene with rubber batons and they are running around the protesters but then with time what i
sentences.zh: 现场，拿着橡胶警棍，他们在抗议者周围奔跑。但随着时间的推移，我

sentences.en: see is that the number of protesters gets larger and larger at one point they even block a street and what the police does is they bring reinforcements they bring army officers
sentences.zh: 看到抗议者的人数越来越多，一度他们甚至封锁了一条街道。警察的做法是调来增援部队，他们带来了配备盾牌的军队军官，

sentences.en: with shields machines that they equipped with water cannons they begin using stun
sentences.zh: 配备水炮的机器，他们开始使用眩晕

sentences.en: grenades there's this scene of complete chaos and this night was the first night
sentences.zh: 手榴弹。现场一片混乱，那一夜是第一次

sentences.en: when hundreds of protesters were ruthlessly beaten they were beaten inside police vans.
sentences.zh: 数百名抗议者遭到残酷殴打，他们在警车里被殴打。

sentences.en: They were beaten in the pretrial detention center.
sentences.zh: 他们在审前拘留中心被殴打。

sentences.en: They were packed like sardines, you know, 36 people in a cell equipped for four people.
sentences.zh: 他们像沙丁鱼一样被塞在一起，你知道，一间只够四个人住的牢房里塞了36个人。

sentences.en: They were not given water or food.
sentences.zh: 他们没有水或食物。

sentences.en: It was basically a huge torture camp.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一个巨大的酷刑营。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And the scene of the crackdown reminded me of Gulag, essentially.
sentences.zh: 镇压的场面让我想起了古拉格，本质上就是那样。

sentences.en: So the goal was to break the spirit of these protesters, and I'm sure even more so than that was to spread the word of these tactics
sentences.zh: 所以目标是摧毁这些抗议者的精神，我敢肯定，更重要的是传播这些战术的消息，

sentences.en: and break the back of these protests altogether.
sentences.zh: 并彻底挫败这些抗议活动。

sentences.en: To scare people off so people weren't even there to come out.
sentences.zh: 为了吓跑人们，让他们甚至不敢出来。

sentences.en: I'm curious how the rest of the world has responded to this pretty brutal crackdown on these protesters.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇世界其他国家对这次针对抗议者的残酷镇压有何反应。

sentences.en: Well, the international community was just shocked by all the images.
sentences.zh: 嗯，国际社会对所有的画面感到震惊。

sentences.en: There were calls to sanction Lukashenko on Belarus.
sentences.zh: 有人呼吁对卢卡申科和白俄罗斯实施制裁。

sentences.en: There were calls not to recognize the results of that election.
sentences.zh: 有人呼吁不要承认选举结果。

sentences.en: And in fact, the results were not recognized by the European Union and many other individual states.
sentences.zh: 事实上，欧盟和许多其他国家都没有承认选举结果。

sentences.en: So at one point, it felt like Lukashenko has been cornered.
sentences.zh: 所以一度感觉卢卡申科被逼到了墙角。

sentences.en: And what he did is that he turned back to Vladimir Putin, basically and publicly asking him for support in this situation.
sentences.zh: 他所做的是转而向弗拉基米尔·普京求助，基本上是公开请求他在这种情况下给予支持。

sentences.en: And how does Putin respond?
sentences.zh: 普京是如何回应的？

sentences.en: For Putin, it is much more beneficial to have Lukashenko so weak that he would only have Putin to rely on.
sentences.zh: 对普京来说，让卢卡申科变得如此虚弱，以至于他只能依赖普京，这更有利。

sentences.en: And thus Putin can easily control him and make him do whatever Putin wants.
sentences.zh: 这样普京就可以轻松控制他，让他做任何普京想做的事。

sentences.en: So he didn't throw a lifeline.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有抛出救命稻草。

sentences.en: He didn't say anything that would directly support him.
sentences.zh: 他没有说任何直接支持他的话。

sentences.en: But he also didn't condemn him.
sentences.zh: 但他也没有谴责他。

sentences.en: And there's no way back, because after what the world has seen, it will take them a long time to forget.
sentences.zh: 而且已经没有回头路了，因为在全世界目睹了这一切之后，他们需要很长时间才能忘记。

sentences.en: So Lukashenko is trapped.
sentences.zh: 所以卢卡申科被困住了。

sentences.en: He is trapped in Putin's hands.
sentences.zh: 他被困在普京的手心里。

sentences.en: Ivan, I'm reminded of what Lukashenko said to the crowd at that rally that you went to a couple of Sundays ago, that if you get rid of me, it will be the end of Belarus.
sentences.zh: 伊万，我想到你几周前周日参加的那场集会上，卢卡申科对人群说的话：如果你们除掉我，那将是白俄罗斯的末日。

sentences.en: But is what you're saying that Lukashenko himself is now so tied up with, so dependent on Russia,
sentences.zh: 但你的意思是，卢卡申科本人现在与俄罗斯捆绑得如此紧密，如此依赖俄罗斯，

sentences.en: that if he stays, it would mean the end of Belarus, at least as an independent country?
sentences.zh: 以至于如果他留下来，就意味着白俄罗斯的终结，至少作为一个独立国家而言是这样？

sentences.en: Well, what he says is that if you get rid of Lukashenko, there will be no Belarus.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他的意思是，如果你们除掉卢卡申科，就不会有白俄罗斯了。

sentences.en: But what he means is that there will be no Lukashenko Belarus.
sentences.zh: 但他真正想说的是，不会再有卢卡申科治下的白俄罗斯了。

sentences.en: And he seems to be willing to sacrifice at least chunks of the Belarusian independence
sentences.zh: 他似乎愿意牺牲掉白俄罗斯独立的一部分，

sentences.en: in order to keep his own Belarus afloat.
sentences.zh: 以维持他自己的白俄罗斯继续存在。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so a Belarus in which he stays in power is going to be a Belarus that's unmistakably aligned with, reliant upon Russia.
sentences.zh: 因此，只要他继续掌权，白俄罗斯就注定会与俄罗斯紧密结盟并依赖于俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Seems like that, yes.
sentences.zh: 看起来确实如此。

sentences.en: And Lukashenko has shown no signs or no willingness to give up power voluntarily, no matter how many people come out to protest against him.
sentences.zh: 而且卢卡申科没有表现出任何自愿放弃权力的迹象或意愿，无论有多少人出来抗议他。

sentences.en: The same day there was this pro-Lukashenko rally, there was another rally.
sentences.zh: 就在那场支持卢卡申科的集会同一天，还有另一场集会。

sentences.en: And that rally looked completely different from what Mr. Lukashenko's rally looked like.
sentences.zh: 那场集会看起来与卢卡申科先生的集会完全不同。

sentences.en: I think that he must go away.
sentences.zh: 我认为他必须下台。

sentences.en: We just need peace and we want just honestly election.
sentences.zh: 我们只是需要和平，我们只想要诚实的选举。

sentences.en: First of all, it was much bigger.
sentences.zh: 首先，那场集会的规模大得多。

sentences.en: It appeared to be the biggest rally in the Belarusian history, with more than 200,000 people showing up.
sentences.zh: 那似乎是白俄罗斯历史上规模最大的集会，有超过20万人参加。

sentences.en: We are protesting here against the violence which is happening against the Belarusian nation.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里抗议针对白俄罗斯民族的暴力行为。

sentences.en: Under no condition can people be beaten up in the police station.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，人们都不应该在警察局里遭到殴打。

sentences.en: And of course, I have never seen anything like that in Belarus.
sentences.zh: 当然，我在白俄罗斯从未见过这样的事情。

sentences.en: Actually, no one has ever seen anything like that in Belarus.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在白俄罗斯，从来没有人见过这样的事情。

sentences.en: Because most people, for 26 years, they could never do anything like that.
sentences.zh: 因为在过去的26年里，大多数人根本无法做任何类似的事情。

sentences.en: So I understand that for your average listener, it might sound like, you know, these people came out and this is something.
sentences.zh: 所以我明白，对于普通听众来说，这听起来可能只是人们走上街头，没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: But still, I mean, that was extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，我的意思是，那是非同寻常的。

sentences.en: This was a historic moment for these people.
sentences.zh: 这对这些人来说是一个历史性的时刻。

sentences.en: And people were chanting, long live Belarus, long live Belarus.
sentences.zh: 人们高呼着：白俄罗斯万岁，白俄罗斯万岁。

sentences.en: Basically telling him that you, Lukashenko, are wrong.
sentences.zh: 基本上是在告诉他：卢卡申科，你错了。

sentences.en: You are not Belarus.
sentences.zh: 你代表不了白俄罗斯。

sentences.en: We are Belarus.
sentences.zh: 我们才是白俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Ivan, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 伊万，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Since we spoke with Ivan, large-scale protests in Belarus have continued, drawing a response from Russia's president, Vladimir Putin,
sentences.zh: 自从我们与伊万交谈以来，白俄罗斯的大规模抗议活动仍在继续，并引起了俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的回应，

sentences.en: who warned the country's citizens against trying to topple Lukashenko, declaring that Russia has formed a special team of security officers to, quote,
sentences.zh: 他警告该国公民不要试图推翻卢卡申科，并宣布俄罗斯已组建了一支特别安全官员小组，用他的原话说是，

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Western countries and several former Soviet republics are seeking to impose sanctions against the leaders of Belarus
sentences.zh: 与此同时，西方国家和几个前苏联加盟共和国正寻求对白俄罗斯领导人实施制裁，

sentences.en: in response to what they called a fraudulent election and Lukashenko's crackdown on peaceful protesters.
sentences.zh: 以回应他们所称的欺诈性选举以及卢卡申科对和平抗议者的镇压。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: We're here to show our support for Kenosha and Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 我们来这里是为了表达对基诺沙和威斯康星州的支持。

sentences.en: The state of Wisconsin's been very good to me.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州对我一直很好。

sentences.en: I love the people.
sentences.zh: 我爱这里的人民。

sentences.en: We've done a lot for the state.
sentences.zh: 我们为这个州做了很多事情。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, President Trump defied the wishes of state and local officials by traveling to Kenosha, Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 周二，特朗普总统无视州和地方官员的意愿，前往威斯康星州基诺沙，

sentences.en: where he met with local law enforcement agents and toured a block of businesses destroyed last week during the unrest over the police shooting of Jacob Blake.
sentences.zh: 在那里他会见了当地执法人员，并参观了上周因雅各布·布莱克被警察枪击引发骚乱而遭到破坏的街区。

sentences.en: Kenosha has been ravaged by anti-police and anti-American riots.
sentences.zh: 基诺沙遭到了反警察和反美暴乱的蹂躏。

sentences.en: They have been hit so hard.
sentences.zh: 他们遭受了沉重的打击。

sentences.en: As he has for days, Trump clearly aligned himself with police and forcefully criticized protesters as lawless.
sentences.zh: 正如他过去几天所做的那样，特朗普明确站在警察一边，并严厉批评抗议者是无法无天的。

sentences.en: And the Times reports that the Biden campaign has raised more than $300 million in August between his campaign and his shared committees with the Democratic Party,
sentences.zh: 据《泰晤士报》报道，拜登竞选团队在8月份通过其竞选活动和与民主党共享的委员会筹集了超过3亿美元，

sentences.en: surpassing previous monthly figures by candidates for both parties.
sentences.zh: 超过了此前两党候选人的月度筹款记录。

sentences.en: Much of the money was raised from small donors and appears to reflect Democrats' enthusiasm for Biden's choice of Senator Kamala Harris as a running mate,
sentences.zh: 大部分资金来自小额捐赠者，这似乎反映了民主党人对拜登选择参议员卡玛拉·哈里斯作为竞选搭档的热情，

sentences.en: which had occurred during the fundraising period.
sentences.zh: 这一选择发生在筹款期间。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barrow.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer,
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，

sentences.en: when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党就陷入了一场激烈、混乱，有时甚至令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 欢迎在任何收听播客的地方订阅。
